scope: A local teaching draft based on one museum photograph. Observation of visible features does not establish ancient function or archaeological context.
prediction_prompt: Inspect the photograph. What can you observe directly, and what would require another source?
expected_source_inputs: A public scene objective that asks for an evidence-grounded judgment
A source title, locator and exact excerpt available to the learner
Candidate claims whose support can be checked directly against the excerpt

independent_checks.description: The attributed museum photograph and its description are available before prediction.
Compare each proposed claim with the photograph and the explicitly identified museum metadata.
Do not infer precise function or burial arrangement from the photograph alone.

source.title: The Met · Hippopotamus ("William")
source.statement: The photograph shows a blue-green hippopotamus-shaped object with dark plant-like motifs. The museum record identifies it as faience, dated ca. 1961–1878 B.C. Material and dating are catalogue information, not measurements made from this photograph.

claims.text: The pictured object has blue-green colouring and dark motifs; its dating comes from the museum record.
The photograph alone proves the precise ritual use of this object.
The photograph establishes how this object was arranged in its original burial.

feedback: Visible features and catalogue claims have different sources. A photograph of an isolated object cannot establish its precise ancient use or original placement; those require contextual evidence.
